title: Guide: learning from a triangle
description: A surviving triangle teaches that one of its nodes must be deleted; one clause rules out every candidate that keeps this triangle. See the guide page "Learning from a counterexample".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The graph of the guide's figures: ten nodes, fifteen edges.
node(1..10).
edge(1,2). edge(1,3). edge(1,4). edge(2,3). edge(2,4). edge(3,4).
edge(4,5). edge(4,6). edge(5,6). edge(6,7). edge(6,8). edge(7,8).
edge(8,9). edge(8,10). edge(9,10).
fragments.description: The graph. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k nodes to delete.
{ del(V) : node(V) } k.
#show del/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): at most k deleted nodes.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check sees which nodes are deleted.
glue(del(V)) :- node(V).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: a triangle none of whose nodes is deleted.
3 { q(V) : node(V) } 3.
:- q(V), del(V).
:- q(U), q(V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
#show q/1.

% The triangle survives as long as none of its nodes is deleted.
relevant(del(V)) :- q(V).
fragments.description: Looks for a triangle that survives the deletions (solver C).

fragments.name: view
fragments.text:
% The graph; deleted nodes filled, the surviving triangle drawn as a clique.
#program scene.
draw(layout(graph)).
draw(node(V))   :- node(V).
draw(edge(U,V)) :- edge(U,V).

#program frame.
draw(attr(node(V), fill, deleted))        :- cand(del(V)).
draw(attr(node(V), fill, clique))         :- cex(q(V)).
draw(attr(edge(U,V), stroke, clique))     :- edge(U,V), cex(q(U)), cex(q(V)).
draw(emph(node(V)))                       :- lit(del(V), _).
draw(note("A triangle survives. One of its ringed nodes must be deleted.")) :- kind(reject).
draw(note("No triangle survives: a solution.")) :- kind(solution).
#show draw/1.
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
